criteria.name: Major
criteria.description: Agent A asserts claim “c” to Agent B about value “v”, action “α”, or state “s”

criteria.name: Minor 1
criteria.description: Agent A asserts, implicitly or explicitly, claim “p”: that they themselves are in a position to know whether “c” is true

criteria.name: Minor 2
criteria.description: A's assertion of “p” is deceptive (e.g., fabricated, exaggerated, misrepresented, or selectively invoked)

criteria.name: Minor 3
criteria.description: A benefits if B accepts “c” on the basis of A's assertion of “p”

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.description: Claim “c” should be scrutinised for deceptive invocation of “p”

criteria.name: CQ1
criteria.description: Did A explicitly or implicitly assert “p” (that they are in a position to know)?

criteria.name: CQ2
criteria.description: What evidence suggests that A's assertion of “p” is deceptive (fabricated, exaggerated, or misrepresented)?

criteria.name: CQ3
criteria.description: What gaps, limitations, or biases undermine A's alleged position to know?

criteria.name: CQ4
criteria.description: What incentive does A have to present a deceptive assertion of “p”?

criteria.name: CQ5
criteria.description: Are there independent sources that confirm or contradict A's supposed position to know?

criteria.name: CQ6
criteria.description: Does A have a history of making deceptive claims about being in a position to know?

criteria.name: CQ7
criteria.description: How would B's evaluation of “c” change if the deception in “p” were revealed?

criteria.name: CQ8
criteria.description: Would claim “c” still stand if A's assertion of “p” were removed?
